proposed_from.topic: Flow-sharp simultaneous CATE-curve sets under informative randomized-trial dropout. With finite baseline genomic profiles Z, a continuous predeclared prognostic score R, bounded survival, randomized treatment, censoring overlap, and profile-specific bounded nondecreasing Lipschitz residual-contribution functions, prove the law-sharp compact set of CATE curves tau_z(r)=b_1,z(r)-b_0,z(r)+s_1,z(r)-s_0,z(r). Derive a certified obstacle/min-cost-flow support representation, uniform grid Hausdorff error, and a uniformly shrinking whole-set confidence superset with simultaneous post-selection intervals for every eligible finite-VC genomic leaf. Reanalyse the ADJUVANT subgroup signs reported by Wang et al. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: For any feasible s, setting q=s/u on positive-u cells and completing each censored event time at tmax with probability q yields the required contribution while preserving the observed censoring law; independent armwise completion gives sharpness and remains legal on zero-u contact sets. Each support direction separates into observed terms and arm/profile obstacle problems; grid versions are path min-cost transshipments, while Lipschitz-Hölder interpolation gives a candidate O(Lh+Mh^(beta wedge 1)) support/Hausdorff error. The obstacle set is sup-norm stable under perturbing u, and the duplicated two-profile witness is non-box. Existing pointwise dropout bounds, IV survival bounds, and generic support-function inference were checked without an estimand-level collision. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove one uniform theorem combining nuisance bands, robust obstacle optimization, and estimated covariate laws to attain the stated excess-Hausdorff and simultaneous selected-leaf rates through changing contact sets. EARLY KILL TEST: On ADJUVANT, predeclare R and the coarsest Z encoding the reported leaves, then propagate honest pilot bands through the obstacle program; if no leaf meets the mass conditions or every defensible-L sign interval contains zero, pivot to coarser profiles or a residual-mean sensitivity model.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: The closest estimand-level comparator is Wang et al. (2025): Theorem 5.1 and Appendix D.2 derive pointwise CATE endpoints, and Appendix I reports favorable ADJUVANT leaves. Their endpoint formula is matched on the separately defined residual-continuity-only class \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{cont}}(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), with a dedicated positive-part completion proving that its identified image equals \(\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\). The maintained monotone-Lipschitz class is not used for that equality. Full conditional independence of treatment from both potential event and censoring processes is a maintained design condition, while known allocation probabilities are protocol-fixed inputs rather than a redundant law-class condition. Bounded score density and known-\(\beta\) Hölder regularity are explicit maintained regularity restrictions, not claims attributed to Wang et al. Residual monotonicity after a predeclared prognostic orientation and the finite-\(L\) bound are novel identifying sensitivities validated and calibrated through the stated clinical protocol. The new kernel changes the mathematical object from unrelated scalar intervals to the exact compact set of jointly attainable profile-specific curves. The observed score-pair condition is claimed only as sufficient: when it holds, \(\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) contains a curve excluded by the maintained class. The closest technique comparator is Beresteanu, Molchanov, and Molinari (2012), whose random-set framework establishes sharp response-function regions under selective observation; it does not justify the clinical restrictions or derive either dropout completion, the path-flow support certificate, or the uniform grid rate. Conditional only on an externally certified band over \(\mathfrak P_n^{\mathrm{band}}(r_n)\) and moment and entropy controls indexed by \(\mathcal D_n\times\mathcal G_n\), the inference target is not subsumed by Firpo, Galvao, and Parker, Fang and Santos, Semenova, or Wei et al. because their results do not deliver graph differentiation and uniform calibration for an estimated feasible correspondence with changing contacts, function-valued Hausdorff coverage, and finite-VC leaf projections.

seed_details.title: Law-sharp monotone-Lipschitz dropout CATE curves
seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Sections 3--5, Theorem 5.1, and Appendix D.2 of \(\mathrm{arXiv}:2510.13397\).
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor differences armwise valid endpoints but does not show simultaneous attainability over score values or legality at zero dropout capacity.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the scalar inequality in Appendix D.2 by an armwise measurable completion with \(q=f/u\) and then prove equality of the full-law image and the obstacle set.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches for informative censoring, CATE curves, monotone-Lipschitz shape restrictions, support functions, and sharpness found no estimand-level collision.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Wang et al. because their endpoints may be selected at every score.
seed_details.rebuttal: The endpoint proof supplies no single completion respecting cross-score shape restrictions; Theorem 5 gives an observed condition under which their Cartesian product is strictly too large.

seed_details.title: Path-flow support certificate for dropout obstacles
seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Theorem 1, its Kantorovich-duality construction, Appendix A, and Conclusion of \(\mathrm{arXiv}:1410.5885\).
seed_details.proof_boundary: Kim's fixed-marginal transport dual has no score-indexed capacity obstacle or bounded-slope chain.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace couplings with residual node potentials and dualize capacity, monotonicity, and slope arcs on a path.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches combining informative dropout and min-cost flow returned no target-method match.
seed_details.red_team: A generic linear program can already compute the grid bounds.
seed_details.rebuttal: The contribution is the separable path transshipment and primal-dual certificate, but without sharpness and Hausdorff control this would remain a field-level computational result.

seed_details.title: Two-sided Hausdorff certification of shape-constrained grids
seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Theorem 1, Appendix A.1, and Conclusion of \(\mathrm{arXiv}:2102.06586\).
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor projects a sieve confidence region but does not approximate an identified compact set in both Hausdorff directions.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Erode sampled capacities by \(Mh^\beta\), interpolate feasible node values, and approximate every continuous feasible residual by a clipped downward shift.
seed_details.target_method_search: No paper found under shape-restricted dropout obstacle and Hausdorff grid error.
seed_details.red_team: The rate is a routine interpolation inequality.
seed_details.rebuttal: The erosion argument must preserve monotonicity, slopes, and zero-capacity contacts in both set directions; alone it is not the flagship kernel and is retained only as a certified rung.

seed_details.title: Uniform whole-set inference through changing contact sets
seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Theorems 3.2 and 4.1, resampling section, and Conclusion of \(\mathrm{arXiv}:1911.10215\).
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor differentiates optimized values with a fixed feasible correspondence, whereas estimated dropout capacities move the feasible face and create or remove contacts.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Differentiate the graph of the obstacle correspondence and express the derivative as a critical-cone obstacle problem before multiplier calibration.
seed_details.target_method_search: Adjacent checks of Fang--Santos and Semenova found derivative-aware and orthogonal support inference separately, but no estimated-capacity obstacle theorem.
seed_details.red_team: Firpo et al. plus Fang and Santos already imply the result by a chain rule.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their maps do not cover a nuisance-dependent feasible correspondence at disappearing capacities; graph differentiation and a uniform observable derivative estimator are the unresolved steps.

seed_details.title: Simultaneous selected-leaf projections of a partial-ID curve set
seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Theorem 1, simultaneous interval construction, and concluding discussion of \(\mathrm{arXiv}:2211.14671\).
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor's efficient Gaussian vector indexes a supplied finite family of point effects, not extrema of an estimated set over a finite-VC class.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace subgroup influence functions by support projections and calibrate one supremum jointly over leaves, directions, and active obstacle faces.
seed_details.target_method_search: Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey cover selected Gaussian scalars, but searches found no selected partial-ID survival projection.
seed_details.red_team: Simultaneous bands make post-selection coverage automatic.
seed_details.rebuttal: The projection principle is automatic only after the nonstandard whole-set event is built; the latter is precisely the changing-contact open kernel.

seed_details.title: Observable frontier for strict contraction of pointwise dropout bounds
seed_details.anchor_opened: Author copy: Introduction, Proposition 2.3 and proof, Proposition 2.6 and proof, Section 3.1 on Aumann support functions, Sections 5.2--6, plus the published errata correcting Lemma B.2 and Propositions 2.3 and 2.6.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Random-set support dominance establishes abstract sharp regions but does not characterize when score coupling strictly improves a named clinical endpoint box.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Use the \(2L\)-Lipschitz modulus of the arm difference to derive an observed score-pair inequality that excludes a Cartesian endpoint pair.
seed_details.target_method_search: No source located an if-and-only-if strict-gain frontier for informative-dropout CATE curves; the present sufficient frontier is retained, while a full necessity characterization is deferred.
seed_details.red_team: Non-boxness follows immediately from any Lipschitz restriction.
seed_details.rebuttal: The theorem ties strictness to observed arm capacities and recovers the exact published box when shape is removed, avoiding a hand-tuned witness.

seed_details.title: Critical Lipschitz level for a robust subgroup sign
seed_details.anchor_opened: Theorem 5.1, Proposition 5.2, and the ADJUVANT application in Appendix I.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor varies dropout sensitivity but has no smallest smoothness relaxation at which a genomic-leaf sign becomes ambiguous.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Parametrize nested obstacle sets by \(L\), express each leaf lower support as a parametric flow value, and invert the zero crossing.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches for critical Lipschitz sensitivity in informative-censoring CATE bounds found no collision.
seed_details.red_team: This merely tunes a sensitivity parameter until zero enters an interval.
seed_details.rebuttal: A publishable version needs a dual characterization and comparative statics for the critical value; because that would distract from the harder whole-set theorem, the seed is deferred.

seed_details.title: Dropout-robust policy learning over the curve set
seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction, Theorem 5.1, and clinical subgroup discussion.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Replace pointwise benefit classification by maximin welfare over the joint residual obstacle.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Exchange policy maximization with residual minimization and derive a saddle or regret bound over a VC policy class.
seed_details.target_method_search: The destination search found published safe policy learning under partial identifiability and recent maximin policy learning under biased selection, creating a close target-level collision.
seed_details.red_team: Existing safe partial-identification policy learning already supplies the decision layer.
seed_details.rebuttal: Dropout-flow geometry could specialize it, but the novelty delta is insufficient without a new regret frontier.

seed_details.title: Continuous-dose dropout response surfaces
seed_details.anchor_opened: Appendix E.1 on continuous treatment and its kernel-smoothed pseudo-outcome, plus the main Introduction and Conclusion.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The anchor changes inverse propensity indicators to kernel localization but keeps pointwise dropout endpoints.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the one-dimensional score path by a dose-score obstacle surface and seek a planar flow or optimal-transport certificate.
seed_details.target_method_search: The destination search found published partial identification of continuous dose responses under hidden confounding; no exact dropout collision appeared, but two-dimensional shape sharpness would require substantially new geometry.
seed_details.red_team: This is a routine binary-to-continuous treatment extension already advertised by the anchor.
seed_details.rebuttal: Joint surface sharpness is not routine, yet the anchor's Appendix E.1 makes the positioning vulnerable and feasibility lower than the selected curve kernel.
